name: Mesoeye

card.summary: Under-eye mesotherapy injections aimed at brighter, fresher-looking eye contours.
card.note: Injection procedure; bruising and infection are reported with mesotherapy.

quick.overview:
Mesoeye is a name for under-eye mesotherapy, a clinic treatment of tiny injections around the eyes. People use it hoping for brighter, less tired-looking skin there.

Sessions are done by a practitioner and usually repeated.
quick.mechanism: A preparation is placed in the superficial skin of the eye area to hydrate and nourish it.
quick.risks: Bruising, swelling, redness and, with poor hygiene, infection are reported for mesotherapy. In the US, injected mixtures are overseen by state medical boards rather than FDA.

lead: Mesoeye, sold as Mesoeye C71, is an injectable under-eye product used in clinics for biorevitalisation of the periorbital area: a practitioner places small superficial injections of a hyaluronic acid and peptide preparation into the thin skin around the eyes. People seek it to soften dark circles and puffiness and to make the eye contour look fresher and less tired.[1][2]

A Russian clinic describes Mesoeye as developed by the American company ABG LAB, with the C71 formulation made by BNC Korea, and registered in Russia in 2016 as an intradermal implant gel. The clinic lists hyaluronic acid, a PeriOrbital Peptide XP2 and hexapeptide 17 among its ingredients and says courses run 3 to 6 sessions.[2] These are clinic descriptions rather than independent studies.

Mesotherapy in general is a technique of intradermal or subcutaneous injection of vitamins, plant extracts, hyaluronic acid and similar substances, with the stated aim of hydrating and nourishing the skin.[1] Dark circles themselves have several causes, including thin lower-eyelid skin, pigmentation, visible blood vessels, fatigue and age-related volume loss, so the look people want to change can arise in different ways.[3]

chain: Tiny injections of hyaluronic acid and peptides into the eye-area skin
Hydration and vessel-support effects claimed by providers
Less puffy, brighter, fresher-looking eye contour
angle.text: Mesoeye is a clinic procedure aimed at brighter, more hydrated under-eye skin with less puffiness. Providers describe a course of several sessions.

infobox: Mesoeye C71 (ABG LAB; formulation by BNC Korea)[2]

paras: Cosmetic mesotherapy was founded by Michel Pistor, and the French press coined the term in 1958; France recognized it as a medical specialty in 1987.[1] A needle-free pressurized variant also exists.[1]

A clinic page describes Mesoeye C71 as combining hyaluronic acid, which it says holds water, with synthetic peptides said to support blood vessels and reduce swelling. Claimed effects include stronger vessel walls, better lymph outflow, hydration, and less puffiness and fewer dark circles. The page says it works best when ageing has just begun and recommends blepharoplasty for deep wrinkles or drooping eyelids.[2]

The clinic describes a topical anaesthetic followed by injection in several passes, taking about 20 minutes, with courses of 3 to 6 sessions spaced up to 10 days apart and a session roughly every six months afterward.[2] It lists contraindications including pregnancy, breastfeeding, clotting and immune disorders, epilepsy, cancer, allergy to components and age under 18.[2]

Reported mesotherapy reactions include bruising, swelling, pain and redness.[1] Infections have been documented after procedures done under unhygienic conditions, and French investigators traced adverse effects to hygiene rather than the treatment itself.[1] For Mesoeye, the clinic says small bruises and eyelid swelling usually resolve within about 5 to 7 days.[2]

No studies found on Mesoeye specifically. Related: a small study of four facial multivitamin mesotherapy sessions in 10 patients found no clinically relevant skin rejuvenation, and cosmetic mesotherapy overall has generally not been tested in standard clinical trials.[1] For dark circles generally, treatments discussed include caffeine and vitamin C eye creams, laser and intense pulsed light, fat transfer and hyaluronic acid fillers.[3]

timeline.event: The French press coins the term mesotherapy.[1]
The French Academy of Medicine recognizes mesotherapy as a specialty.[1]
Mesoeye C71 registered in Russia as an intradermal implant gel, per a clinic description.[2]
